chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Nawfali, from al-Yaqubi, from Isa ibn Abdullah, from Suleiman ibn Ja'far, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And We send down water from the sky according to a measure, then We settle it in the earth, and We are able to take it away.' He said: 'Meaning the water of the ravines.'
ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'We settle it in the earth' in Surah al-Mu'minun refer to according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the phrase 'We settle it in the earth' in Surah al-Mu'minun (23:18) as a specific reference to the water of the 'aqiq' (ravines or wadis). This interpretation highlights the Shia scholarly understanding of divine hydrological management, where water is not merely present but actively stored and preserved within the earth's natural channels and reservoirs by God's power.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Abbas Bin Marouf, from Al Nowfaly from Al Yaqouby, from Isa Bin Abdullah, from Suleyman Bin Ja’far having said:

‘Abu Abdullahasws said regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [23:18] And We send down water from the sky according to a measure, then We Settle it in the earth, and We are able to Take it away. So heasws said: ‘Meaning the water of the ravines’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma’ruf from Nawfaliy from al-Ya‘qubiy from “Isa ibn ‘Abd Allah from Sulayman ibn Ja‘far who has said the following:

“About the meaning of the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘We sent water from the sky in measures and placed it on earth and We have the power to take it away,’ [23:18] abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It means canyons and ravines.’”
